q1.q: Will solar work during the monsoon?
q1.a: Yes, but it makes less power on cloudy days. Systems are sized on yearly averages, so the sunny months make up for it.

q2.a: Only if you have frequent power cuts or live off the grid. With reliable power, an on-grid system with net metering is cheaper and needs no battery.

q3.q: How much roof space do I need?
q3.a: About 100 sq ft for every 1 kW. A typical home needs 2 to 3 kW, so 200 to 300 sq ft of shade-free roof.

q4.a: Central subsidies for homes are paid directly into your bank account after installation and inspection. Check the Schemes page for current rules.

q5.q: I live in an apartment. Can I still go solar?
q5.a: Yes. Your residents’ association can install solar on the common roof for lifts, lights and pumps, which lowers maintenance charges for everyone.

reason.reliable: Your power is reliable, so an on-grid system with net metering gives the best savings with no battery to replace.
reason.occasional: Cuts are rare, so on-grid with net metering is the best value. You can add a small battery later.
reason.frequent: Frequent cuts mean you need backup. A hybrid system powers your home and charges a battery for when the grid is down.
reason.remote: Without a dependable grid, an off-grid system with batteries keeps your lights and fans running day and night.
reason.apartment: Flats share a roof. The best route is solar on the common roof through your residents’ association, which cuts common charges for every flat.
reason.business: Your daytime use matches when the sun shines. A larger on-grid system pays back fast at commercial tariffs.
reason.businessBackup: Cuts hurt business. A hybrid system keeps essentials running and still lowers your bill.
reason.farmer: A solar pumpset runs your motor straight from the sun during the day, with central and state support under PM-KUSUM.
